title: Variable Neighborhood Trust Region Search
text: R package implements variable neighborhood trust region search (VNTRS) algorithm nonlinear global optimization, based Bierlaire et al. (2009) “Heuristic Nonlinear Global Optimization”. method combines neighborhood exploration trust-region framework search solution space efficiently. can terminate local search early iterates converge toward previously visited local optimum improvement within current region unlikely. algorithm can also used identify multiple local optima. package implementation differs aspects Bierlaire et al. (2009) follows:

title: Variable Neighborhood Trust Region Search
text: Specify function f computes objective value. may also return gradient Hessian. Omitted derivatives approximated finite differences. Call vntrs::vntrs(f = f, npar = npar, minimize = minimize), npar number parameters f minimize determines whether f minimized (minimize = TRUE, default) maximized (minimize = FALSE). Optionally, algorithm can tuned setting control arguments, see help("vntrs") details.

title: Variable Neighborhood Trust Region Search
text: example minimizes six-hump camel function [−3,3]×[−2,2][-3, 3] \times [-2, 2]. domain, function two global minima four additional local minima.
code: library(vntrs) set.seed(1) camel <- function(x) {   (4 - 2.1 * x[1]^2 + x[1]^4 / 3) * x[1]^2 + x[1] * x[2] + (-4 + 4 * x[2]^2) * x[2]^2 } optima <- vntrs(   f = camel, npar = 2,   lower = c(-3, -2), upper = c(3, 2), # search bounds   collect_all = TRUE,                 # also collect local optima   neighborhoods = 10                  # number of neighborhoods ) optima #>            p1         p2      value global #> 1 -0.08984203  0.7126564 -1.0316285   TRUE #> 2  0.08984201 -0.7126564 -1.0316285   TRUE #> 3  1.70360672 -0.7960836 -0.2154638  FALSE #> 4 -1.70360674  0.7960836 -0.2154638  FALSE #> 5 -1.60710473 -0.5686515  2.1042503  FALSE #> 6  1.60710475  0.5686517  2.1042503  FALSE

code: ### Example 1: Rosenbrock function; one global minimum; no local minima set.seed(1) rosenbrock <- function(x) 100 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)^2 + (1 - x[1])^2 vntrs(f = rosenbrock, npar = 2) #>   p1 p2        value global #> 1  1  1 1.681733e-16   TRUE  ### Example 2: Six-hump camel function; two global minima; four local minima set.seed(1) camel <- function(x) {   (4 - 2.1*x[1]^2 + x[1]^4/3) * x[1]^2 + x[1]*x[2] + (-4 + 4*x[2]^2) * x[2]^2 } vntrs(   f = camel, npar = 2,   lower = c(-3, -2), upper = c(3, 2), # search bounds   collect_all = TRUE,                 # also collect local optima   neighborhoods = 10                  # number of neighborhoods ) #>            p1         p2      value global #> 1 -0.08984203  0.7126564 -1.0316285   TRUE #> 2  0.08984201 -0.7126564 -1.0316285   TRUE #> 3  1.70360672 -0.7960836 -0.2154638  FALSE #> 4 -1.70360674  0.7960836 -0.2154638  FALSE #> 5 -1.60710473 -0.5686515  2.1042503  FALSE #> 6  1.60710475  0.5686517  2.1042503  FALSE

title: vntrs 0.3.0
text: Reorganized optional arguments vntrs(). Renamed argument tolerance identical_tolerance clarify identifies identical optima. Made duplicate-optimum detection scale-free comparing relative component-wise parameter differences. Added interruption_gradient_tolerance control gradient-norm threshold used premature interruption. Now samples initialization points across finite parameter bounds. init_min init_max remain fallback parameters without finite bounds. Expanded parameter documentation explanations recommended values. Improved initialization objective non-finite randomly generated starting point. Now sorts returned optima best worst objective value. Reduced objective-function evaluations delaying numerical gradients trial step accepted reusing available values gradients. # vntrs 0.2.2 Replaced absolute gradient convergence check scaled gradient criterion. Reworked missing-derivative handling. Added damped-BFGS trust-region models reuse local curvature across continued searches.
